insight: The hydration break statistics for South Korea in the 2026 FIFA World Cup reveal some interesting trends. On average, the team tends to gain momentum after a break, with a slight increase in their performance in 4 out of 6 instances, resulting in a minimal average decrease in momentum of -0.033 minutes. However, when South Korea is pressing before a break, they tend to struggle, losing momentum at an average rate of -0.300 minutes per break, and failing to regain it in the only instance this occurred. In contrast, when they are not pressing before a break, they are able to maintain or slightly increase their momentum, with an average increase of +0.020 minutes per break, suggesting that breaks can be a valuable opportunity for the team to regroup and refocus.
